title: Redundancy in Learning
hook: You read the book. You nodded along. Try explaining it tomorrow and it's mostly gone.
statement: Learn things more than one way so they actually stick.
explainer: Reading once gives you recognition, not recall. You'll nod if you see it again but can't pull it up when you need it. Writing it, saying it, and using it lock it in.
sop: Take in the material once, however you like best.
Within 24 hours, reinforce it another way, like writing or explaining it.
Count your Modes of Engagement for each thing you're learning.
Keep a list of topics to explain to someone this week.
Revisit anything you still can't explain simply.
equation_example: Count your Modes of Engagement. Read it, that's 1. Wrote a summary, 2. Explained it out loud, 3. Actually used it, 4. At 1 mode, Retention fades in days. At 4, it's still there weeks later. More modes means it lasts.
question: Pick one thing you learned this week and explain it out loud to someone today.
closing_statement: Recalling something beats just recognizing it.
